name: Boeing 747
summary: Four-engined jumbo with the iconic upper-deck hump; US examples are now almost all freighters with Atlas, UPS, Kalitta and National.

wings: Upturned winglets on the -400; long raked wingtips on the -8
engines: Four engines on separate underwing pylons
fuselage: Distinctive raised upper-deck hump behind the cockpit (short on -400F freighters, long on passenger and -8 versions)
Freighters have no cabin windows and a hinged nose door
Four main-gear bogies under the belly

tellTales: Hump on the forward upper fuselage
Four engines under a large swept wing
Huge widebody with four main-gear bogies

confusedWith.howToTell: The 747 has four engines and an upper-deck hump; the 777 has two enormous engines, a uniform tube and six-wheel bogies.
The 747 has a low wing with engines below it and a hump only over the front; the C-5 has a high wing, a T-tail and a full-length upward-opening visor nose.

usCount.source: Freighter fleet data (Atlas ~60 incl. 747-8F, UPS ~40, Kalitta ~22, National ~4; Atlas Air Worldwide / Cargo Facts / planespotters.net)
